title: 人有时候会欺负你，一定是你示弱了

coverage.excluded_asr_tail: S00090 crosses the audited 149.234649-second endpoint; S00091-S00117 are wholly beyond it. S00090-S00117 are excluded from claims and timeline evidence.

timeline.summary: He uses a dog-biting metaphor and physical punishment to argue that people bully someone after detecting weakness.
He applies the idea to dates, first treating eye-contact avoidance as weakness, then describing directly asking about disengagement and ending a date when communication is poor.
He says willingness to lose the interaction is necessary for boundaries and links neediness to placing women too centrally in life.
He urges attention to other enjoyable parts of life rather than fixation on messages, love or failed dates, and claims fearlessness makes success easier.
He repeats that one must risk losing a date to say 'you should go home' when uncomfortable, then claims fear of loss leads to ongoing disrespect.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He uses physically punishing a dog as a metaphor for stopping disrespect early and claims people bully someone only after sensing weakness.
claims.conditions: Unsupported universal claim and violent animal analogy; it must not be literalized or generalized.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: On a disengaged date, he describes asking whether the other person is unhappy and, if communication remains poor, saying the date should end.
claims.conditions: Ending an interaction is acceptable when done calmly and safely; it does not prove the other person is disrespectful or manipulative.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He links neediness to placing women too centrally in life and recommends maintaining other enjoyable experiences so one is less consumed by messages or failed dates.
claims.conditions: A broad self-regulation framing, not proof that detachment causes romantic success.

claims.speaker: Mikey
claims.statement: He says fear of losing a woman prevents a man from voicing discomfort or ending a date and then claims this invites continuing disrespect.
claims.conditions: The boundary-setting portion must be separated from the unsupported claim that fear necessarily causes another person's disrespect.

speaker_attribution.speaker: Mikey
speaker_attribution.basis: One visible channel host speaks throughout, and the wording matches formal mikey-youtube-live-010.

visual_findings: All 50 sampled frames show the same black-shirt speaker in one purple-lit livestream setup with added subtitles and a stream overlay.
No dog, date partner, live interaction or independent evidence of disrespect or outcome is shown.
